deep.reconstruction:
This page is a sheet of drawings with letter and number labels only; it contains no text. It belongs to Grothendieck's 1983-84 study of pseudoline systems (arrangements of simple closed curves in the real projective plane P^2(R) in which any two curves meet exactly once, crossing there). It is drawn on the back of a 1982 computer job listing.

(1) Top centre: P^2 is drawn as a disk whose boundary circle has antipodal points identified. Five pseudolines run across it, with endpoints labelled 1..5 on one half of the boundary and 1'..5' on the opposite half, so k and k' are antipodal. Dashed light-green and dark-green circles are doubled copies of the boundary, apparently tracking which half of the boundary is glued to which. Some cells are shaded orange. These are mainly triangular cells and cells adjacent to particular lines, presumably the cells relevant to a local move (a triangle flip) or to a sweep.

(2) Top left: one line is drawn twice-crossing the curve near it (a lens), together with a hyperbola-like curve. This is probably a non-example or a picture of a deformation.

(3) Middle: one pseudoline is drawn as the diameter ab of a small disk. Two further arcs from a to b are drawn, one light green and one dark green. Arrows lead from this disk to two pictures marked '~'. Each picture shows the two halves (red boundary semicircle plus green arc) regrouped and redrawn as a 'D' shape. In the 'D', the straight side is the segment ab, carrying the transported labels 2'..5' going up or 2..5 going down, with arrows showing direction. The content: cutting P^2 along one pseudoline L gives a closed disk. Its boundary is the double cover of L, consisting of two copies of the segment ab traversed in opposite directions. The two half-disks of the picture are glued along their outer arcs by the antipodal map. The page is working out explicitly how labels and orientations are carried across this regluing.

(4) Bottom left, in pencil: two circles, each with arcs α and β joining a and b, with rotation arrows ω and the roles of a and b swapped between the upper and lower circles. This is the same gluing written abstractly. The arc α of one copy is matched to β of the other with an orientation reversal, as in the antipodal identification.

(5) Bottom middle, in pencil: a half-disk cut by the segment α/β, and larger circles. These are further attempts at the same cut-and-reglue.

(6) Bottom right: a rectangle containing orange strands and one red horizontal mid-line with green markings, and next to it a rectangle split into two rectangles along green edges. Removing a disk from P^2, or using a strip model, gives a Möbius band, drawn as a rectangle whose ends are glued with a flip. The pseudolines become strands across it, essentially a wiring-diagram picture. Cutting along the distinguished line (the middle red/green segment) splits it into pieces, shown as the two stacked rectangles.

Overall, the page establishes the elementary topological normal forms for drawing a pseudoline arrangement once one line is chosen as 'the line at infinity': the disk model, the half-disk / 'D' model, and the rectangle / Möbius model. This is presumably to encode arrangements combinatorially, as on the neighbouring pages, which list boundary label sequences such as 1 2 3 4 5 1' 2' ... with a and b.
errors: The top-left sketch shows two curves crossing twice (a lens). In a pseudoline system that is not allowed, so it must be a non-example or an intermediate picture rather than a valid configuration. Nothing on the page asserts it is valid.
Nothing can be checked as a claim; the drawings are consistent with the standard topology of P^2: P^2 minus a line is an open disk, and P^2 minus an open disk is a Möbius band.

ideas.what: Representing a pseudoline arrangement in a disk with antipodal boundary identification, with endpoints labelled k / k'
ideas.modern_name: Disk (hemisphere) model of P^2(R) for pseudoline arrangements

ideas.what: Cutting P^2 along one pseudoline to get a disk whose boundary is the doubled line, and redrawing it as a 'D' with explicit transport of labels and orientations
ideas.modern_name: Affine chart / line at infinity; cut-open disk, as used for wiring diagrams and allowable sequences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman (1980, wiring diagrams); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, early 1980s)

ideas.what: Möbius-band / rectangle model with strands for the pseudolines, cut along one distinguished line
ideas.modern_name: Wiring diagram / Möbius strip representation of arrangements

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a set of exploratory drawings of standard models of pseudoline arrangements in P^2(R): disk with antipodal boundary, cut-open disk, and Möbius rectangle. Everything here is classical (Levi, Ringel, Grünbaum, Goodman–Pollack). The only point of mild interest is that it documents Grothendieck independently working out these normal forms in 1983-84.
transcription_corrections: The bottom label of the top-centre figure is 1' (antipodal to the top label 1), not a stray character.
Left boundary labels of the top-centre figure are 2, 3, 4, 5 (2 near the top left); right labels are 4', 3', 2' (and 5'), reading downward.
'~' symbols sit between the round pictures and the 'D'-shaped pictures, marking the two representations as equivalent.

Bottom-left pencil labels: β at the top, ω with a rotation arrow, a and b swapped between the upper and lower circles, α on the lower arc of the top circle and β on the upper arc of the bottom circle.
Arrows (an upward arrow beside 5' 4' 3' 2', a downward arrow beside 2 3 4 5) indicate the direction of label transport along the segment ab in the 'D' figures.
